title: SCAM DO NOT SIGN UP

author: Kylisha28

title: Requirement to confirm diagnosis to proceed
body:
In a time where ‘national neurodivergence registers’ are apparently all the rage, if you’re going to have an app’s usability tied to immediate confirmation as to whether you “have” ADHD, “think” you have it, or “just want to improve your executive functioning, in the same way Period Tracking app developers need to be IMMEDIATELY up front with users re centralisation of user data, etc; ADHD app developers need to be very clear: what data they can see; who else may be able to access this were certain bad actors to obtain a government order to release such, etc.

And if they can’t do that, they need to at least change the option to clarify ‘if you pick no, the app may change it’s approach to assistance/suggestions for you’ or ‘if you pick no, this will not impact the app’s ability to assist you - even if you have ADHD’. At least help users protect themselves in such uncertain times, while understanding whether the app is designed to be useful for them while they are potentially doing so.

author: Red-arms

title: Scammy, Misleading, and Unethical Subscription Practices
body:
Originally, I signed up for a free trial of Clarity ADHD only to find out later that I was secretly subscribed to Fabulous App as well without my knowledge or consent. I never even had Fabulous installed yet was charged $62.99 after the trial ended. There was no clear warning or confirmation that I was subscribing to multiple services.

Looking into it, I found tons of other people with the exact same experience, all unknowingly charged after their trial. Canceling was unnecessarily difficult, requiring multiple steps to cancel both Clarity and Fabulous separately.

This is a predatory and deceptive business model that takes advantage of people who need help with ADHD. No ethical mental health app should operate this way. If you’re considering signing up, DON’T. Save yourself the frustration and money.

author: universe93

title: Unaffordable
body:
ADHD medications, appointments with doctors and psychiatrists, therapy, supplements - as if all this wasn’t costly enough. I think this is a great app, it has everything I’ve been looking for in an app catered for ADHD brains, it’s just a shame that I can’t afford it. I’m sure the developers have justifications for the cost. But I just cannot afford 60AUD per month or 150AUD per year for it, on top of living expenses, medical costs, etc. Honestly, it makes me so sad that anything that could help me learn to manage my ADHD is out of my financial reach, especially since I already struggle with my finances due to ADHD. 😭 

In saying that, if you are in a stable financial position, then the cost of this app won’t be an issue for you!

title: Confusing App
body: This app has some helpful tips and turns tasks into a game… but I can’t follow the reasoning behind the ‘journeys’ and it’s not intuitive to navigate around the app. Especially when there are unhelpful links and ads to other related apps on the main user page designed to take you out of the app and buy their other products. I don’t want to see those in an app I’ve paid a lot of money for - especially if I tried them already! This app is just not user friendly for ADHD organisation, it’s more of an education tool. I repeat tasks and work projects daily, weekly or monthly but there’s no way to plan a whole day, week, month and then focus on individual tasks. And no calendar. Everything in the rest of my life syncs to google calendar so I can visually organise my day/week/month and it’s odd that an ADHD app makes me manually add tasks each day. I recommend you do a trial but don’t pay a subscription unless this app is really helping you.
